cards.name: Floating-body 1T-DRAM (Z-RAM lineage) on U.S. SOI
cards.what_it_is: Recreate a Z-RAM/Toshiba-FBC-style floating-body 1T cell (charge held in the body of an SOI MOSFET and read as a threshold-voltage shift) on a GlobalFoundries SOI flow (45RFSOI-class at a U.S. GF fab [UNVERIFIED-training]; note 22FDX is made in Dresden, not the U.S.). Product: standalone 2-4 Gb DDR3/DDR4-interface dies for legacy-DRAM buyers, or last-level-cache macros.
cards.why_it_could_work: No storage capacitor, so only 1-2 extra masks on a logic SOI flow instead of a DRAM stack-capacitor module. Depreciated SOI capacity exists in the U.S. On paper an 8F2 cell at 45nm gives 0.031 Gb/mm2 and about $24/GB including test (A3_device_params A3-01), which is below today's DDR5 spot (~$27/GB). The 2026 capacitor-less revival (NEO 3D X-DRAM PoC) shows the industry still wants capacitor-less DRAM.

cards.name: Thyristor RAM revival (T-RAM TCCT / Kilopass VLT)
cards.what_it_is: Revive the thin capacitively-coupled thyristor (TCCT) T-RAM cell, or Kilopass's vertical-layered-thyristor (VLT) cross-point cell, as a capacitor-less SRAM/DRAM replacement on a U.S. line (a GF U.S. SOI flow or SkyWater 90nm FD-SOI [UNVERIFIED-training]). Product: cache macros, or a standalone DRAM-replacement die.
cards.why_it_could_work: A PNPN latch stores the bit with built-in gain, so it reads fast (1-2 ns claimed) and needs no capacitor. The VLT marketing claim (4F2, no refresh, 'DRAM cost minus 45%') computes to ~$2.8/GB, DRAM-cost parity (A3-02b). A planar TCCT at 10F2/32nm computes to ~$18/GB. The earliest Stanford NDR-cell patents (~1998) have expired, so IP is no longer the barrier [UNVERIFIED-training].

cards.name: Si gain-cell eDRAM (GCRAM) IP for U.S. trailing-node SoCs
cards.subbranch: Capacitor-less silicon DRAM: 2T/3T gain-cell eDRAM in logic
cards.what_it_is: A memory-IP company that builds and licenses a logic-compatible (zero extra masks) 2T/3T silicon gain-cell eDRAM compiler, first for SkyWater S130/S90 FD-SOI and GlobalFoundries 12LP+ (Malta NY). It replaces 6T SRAM in edge-AI activation buffers, image-sensor line buffers and FPGA block RAM. Revenue is a per-node license fee plus royalty, sold through the foundry IP catalog, as SkyWater already does for Weebit ReRAM.
cards.why_it_could_work: SRAM scaling has stalled, and 6T SRAM costs ~$80-120/GB of die area at every node from 28nm to N2 (A3-06). A gain cell at ~50% of 6T area computes to ~$47/GB area-equivalent at 28nm, about 40% memory-area savings with lower leakage per bit. Foundries pay for differentiated embedded memory: GF bought Renesas CBRAM, and SkyWater qualified third-party ReRAM. Si read devices are fast; oxide gain cells (A1-01) are slow (DATE 2026).

cards.subbranch: SRAM-at-scale on trailing nodes: on-chip memory supply for U.S.-fab ASICs

It is built on the BSD-licensed OpenRAM compiler and sold as a SaaS subscription (hosted macro generator, characterized Liberty/LEF/GDS libraries, CI regression) plus per-tapeout support, listed on the ChipFoundry Marketplace.
cards.why_it_could_work: OpenRAM is alive (v1.2.50, 2026-10-27), but only 1-4 KB prebuilt sky130 macros exist. Small teams cannot afford commercial memory compilers ($50k-$200k+ per node [UNVERIFIED-training]). ChipFoundry runs an IP marketplace on an active SkyWater shuttle flow. The work is Python, CI and web tooling, which is the founder's skill set.

It is sold to air-gapped defense/IC RAG and SIEM buyers as hardware plus an annual software subscription.
cards.why_it_could_work: The APU runs nearest-neighbour search inside SRAM, so a billion-vector index needs far less DRAM bandwidth and capacity per query than on CPUs/GPUs. With DRAM/HBM at 2-3x 2025 prices, DRAM GB per QPS matters. A 2025 Cornell study reported GPU-class retrieval at much lower energy [UNVERIFIED-training]. GSI is small (~$20M revenue) and needs software channel partners, and the integration is mostly software.

cards.name: Cryo-CMOS gain-cell eDRAM IP for quantum-computer control
cards.what_it_is: A memory-IP and test-chip business offering Si gain-cell eDRAM macros characterized at 4 K and 77 K for cryo-CMOS qubit-controller ASICs, fabbed on GF 12LP+ (Malta NY) or SkyWater 90nm FD-SOI. Revenue is NRE plus licenses from quantum hardware teams and national-lab programs.
cards.why_it_could_work: At cryogenic temperatures subthreshold leakage collapses, so Si gain-cell retention rises from microseconds to seconds or more [UNVERIFIED-training]. That makes refresh nearly free while keeping ~2x SRAM density and very low static power. This matters because the 4 K stage has only ~1 W of cooling budget. Superconducting memories (SFQ/JMRAM) remain far less dense.
